title: A Cover for the Border
premise: Sable Fairweather, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Trust—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent a decade erasing people and paper trails. When a stranger named Ivo Kessler repays a favor Sable never performed, he drags her into a plot by her own employers: a staged 'accident' at Frankfurt's central exchange timed to open markets in chaos. As Sable assembles an unlikely crew of discarded assets—a forger, a defected analyst, a teenage hacker she once orphaned on paper—she discovers the favor was real, paid years ago by a version of herself she buried. In the end, Sable chooses exposure over invisibility, stopping the attack minutes before opening bell and trading her polished lie for a fragile, chosen family.
about_author: Felix Voss is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent six years working contracts across Central Europe before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be nobody.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. We meet her mid-extraction in Vienna, burning an identity for a client while narrating her three rules of invisibility. She returns to her flat, checks the go-bag out of habit, and finds a note slipped under the door: a debt acknowledged, signed with a name she doesn't know. Beat: controlled loneliness.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The stranger, Ivo Kessler, waits in her safehouse café with proof: a rescue in Riga eight years ago that Sable has no memory of performing. He says the Meridian Trust is planning something at the Frankfurt exchange and someone inside wants it stopped. She dismisses him—but keeps his burner number. Beat: unease beneath skepticism.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable pulls her own files from the Trust's archive using an old access ritual, hunting the Riga operation. She finds her signature on documents she never signed—and a redacted project codenamed LANTERN. Her handler, Director Ashe, watches her too closely at debrief. Beat: the floor tilting; her past may not be hers.

chapters.title: The Favor That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback chapter to Riga: a young analyst, terrified, saved by a woman with Sable's face and voice—who then vanished without a word. Ivo spent eight years finding her. He reveals LANTERN's shape: a gas 'accident' at the exchange, blamed on a dead patsy, timed for market open. Beat: gratitude curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Three Rules, Broken
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs counter-surveillance and confirms she's being followed by Trust security—Ashe knows she looked. Forced to choose, she burns her own legend and goes dark, breaking all three of her rules in one night. Beat: terror and strange exhilaration of becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Forger's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sable recruits Mirela, a brilliant document forger living quietly above a Bucharest print shop, whom Sable once erased from Interpol's lists as payment for a job. Mirela agrees instantly—not out of loyalty, but because she's been waiting eight years for Sable to need her. Beat: first thread of found family.

chapters.title: LANTERN
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Working from fragments, the team reconstructs LANTERN: not one attack but a coordinated pair—a physical release in the exchange building and a data spoof to trigger automated sell-offs. The patsy is already hired; the date is eleven days out. Beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Sable tracks down Denny, now seventeen, the son of a man she erased—the boy left legally nonexistent, living off-grid and brilliant with network intrusion. Their reunion is hostile; he hates what she did to his father. She offers him a way to matter instead. Beat: guilt meeting its invoice.

chapters.title: Inside the Trust
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using old friendships, Ivo gets close to a mid-level Trust officer who confirms LANTERN's author: Deputy Director Corven, Ashe's rival, building a catastrophe to seize control of the Trust itself. The officer warns them: Ashe isn't innocent either. Beat: the enemy has two faces.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Quietly
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Advance team arrives in Frankfurt under cover identities Mirela forged. They map the exchange's HVAC and server floors, discover the gas system was serviced last month by a shell company tied to Corven. First surveillance near-miss with Trust watchers. Beat: claustrophobic tension, ticking clock established.

chapters.title: What Ashe Knows
chapters.summary: Sable risks contact with Director Ashe through a cutout. Ashe denies ordering LANTERN but admits she let it proceed—Corven offered her retirement in exchange for blindness. She gives Sable one asset: the patsy's name. Beat: betrayal layered on betrayal; no clean side.

chapters.title: The Patsy
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny and Ivo find the patsy, a desperate ex-mercenary told he's doing a 'drill.' Rather than turn him in, they recruit him—he knows the building's service corridors. Denny, working beside men like his father might have been, softens toward Sable. Beat: anger giving way to belonging.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Planning montage: Mirela forges contractor credentials, Denny maps the data-spoof entry point, Ivo handles the human element. Sable realizes the team functions like nothing she's ever had—a unit held together by choice, not contract. Then Trust security raids their safehouse early. Beat: warmth interrupted by violence.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Action chapter, rotating POV. The raid scatters the team; Mirela is captured carrying the forged credentials. Sable must decide: abort and run, or escalate. She reads the raid's precision and understands—it wasn't Corven. It was the Trust testing whether she'd run. Beat: sacrifice made concrete; the cost becomes personal.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable offers herself to Ashe in exchange for Mirela's release—a recorded confession to decades of deniable work. Ashe takes the deal but tips her off privately: Corven has moved the timeline up. The attack is now four days away, before any authority can react. Beat: self-erasure reversed; she spends her secrets to save someone else.

chapters.title: The Spoof
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny infiltrates the exchange's network through a maintenance vendor, planting a kill-switch against the sell-off algorithm. He finds evidence the data attack is further along than believed—already armed, awaiting a single authorization packet. Beat: competence as love; the kid proves himself.

chapters.title: Two Faces at Dawn
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confronts Corven at a private club, wearing a wire, buying time by pretending to defect. Corven monologues just enough: the accident will look like terrorism, the Trust will be 'forced' to assume emergency powers across European operations. Ivo barely escapes. Beat: villain revealed in full; stakes become institutional, not just physical.

chapters.title: Seventeen Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Final assembly: positions assigned, contingencies argued, goodbyes half-said. Sable admits to the team she doesn't know if the Riga rescue was really her—and Ivo tells her it doesn't matter, because the person in this room is the one who showed up. Beat: quiet before the storm; identity resolved through action, not memory.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Climax, rapid POV rotation. The team hits the exchange in the pre-dawn hours: Denny kills the algorithm remotely, the patsy seals the gas lines, Ivo holds the control room, Mirela's credentials get Sable to the authorization terminal seconds after Corven's packet launches. She kills it at 08:59. Corven, present to watch his masterpiece, is arrested by Ashe's people—she chose a side at last. Beat: breathless convergence.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The world believes a maintenance incident was averted; only five people know how close it came. The Trust offers Sable a promotion built on her confession's silence. She declines, walks out with nothing but the go-bag—and leaves it behind at the door. Beat: liberation through subtraction.

chapters.title: A Table With Chairs
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, one scene each. Three months later: Mirela's print shop becomes a front for a tiny agency that helps the erased reappear; Denny enrolls in school under a name Mirela forged beautifully; Ivo tends bar downstairs. Sable, legally Sable for the first time, learns to be found. Beat: belonging as a daily practice.

chapters.title: The Favor, Returned
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, coda. A stranger appears at the print shop with a note: a debt acknowledged, echoing the one that started everything. Sable smiles, packs light—no go-bag this time—and steps out with her family watching her back. The last line mirrors the first rule of invisibility, rewritten: never be so invisible that no one comes looking. Beat: full-circle hope.
